def.brief:
Write ONE new file, SELFHOSTING.md at the repository root: brief source-maintainer guidance for future sessions that change this chongdae checkout with its own released toolchain. It is real guidance, not a code change. Change no other file: README.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, plugin.json, .claude-plugin/plugin.json and .codex-plugin/plugin.json carry someone else's uncommitted edits and must stay byte-identical (the check hashes them). Do not commit. Link, do not duplicate: point to AGENTS.md, README.md (only anchors present in both HEAD and the working tree, e.g. #versioning, #self-check, #providers, #limits), skills/run/SKILL.md, hunsu.json and hunsu.lock.json; never restate the run workflow. At most 90 lines. No machine paths (no /Users/...): call a plugin root `<root>` and say it comes from the SessionStart line. Every sentence must be true of this checkout; verify each against the file named below and leave out anything you cannot verify.

Facts to cover (verified by the session; sources in parentheses):
1. Declared roles (hunsu.json `roles`, identical in hunsu.lock.json): planner = session; implementer = hacheong member dakdol on host codex; nitpick = teujip on claude; quibble = sibi on claude; newbie = chojja on codex; verifier = dwitbuk eyes_worker.py on claude; reviewer = `dwitbuk review --target .`, which chongdae runs at close; coherence = `mangsang impact --target .`. No role passes --model, so each host's default model answers. Reporters: hunsu `check --findings`, chongdae `report --since {since}`, mangsang `impact --findings`, all with `--target .`. `capabilities`: loopback and network are both `session`. The five `resolutions` are all `reviewed: false` (`hunsu policy` prints them).
2. Released versions locked (hunsu.lock.json `plugins`): hunsu 1.15.1, chongdae 1.24.0, mangsang 1.19.3, jokbo 1.8.1, hacheong 1.12.1, dwitbuk 1.16.0, installed at project scope for Claude Code. The SessionStart hook line names each locked root; call engines at those roots, never through a glob over the plugin cache.
3. Python: hunsu.json `engines` requires python >=3.11 (and claude-code >=2.1). The released 1.24.0 manifests disagree: HEAD `plugin.json` and HEAD `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` say >=3.9, HEAD `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` says >=3.11 (`git show HEAD:<file>`); the three must agree before the next release (README#versioning).
4. A prospective run: before any write, `python3 "<chongdae root>/chongdae.py" init --session --goal "..." --target .` with the locked root; the chongdae PreToolUse hook refuses Edit/Write until a run is open. Add a task before its work; work that predates its task is `adopt`ed with a --why naming who wrote it. Commit only a task's own paths, subject `run-<id>/<task> (session): ...`, never `git add -A`; edits made outside a run stay unstaged as someone's prior work. A documentation-only change needs no tests writer: say so on the task and decide it by link/manifest checks. `close` runs the reviewer. Version bump, push and release are separate steps (README#versioning).
5. Source vs installed: this checkout is the source of the next chongdae; the orchestrator is the installed locked release, never this checkout's ./chongdae.py. An engine run from a working source names its version `+g<sha>[-dirty]` (chongdae.py `source_revision`), and a run's `.chongdae/run-*/state.json` `written_by` shows which engine wrote it. Testing the working source (`python3 test_chongdae.py`, AGENTS.md) is not orchestration.
6. N manages N+1: the locked release N (now chongdae 1.24.0) orchestrates every change to this source, which becomes N+1. N+1 manages nothing, not even the change after it, until it is bumped in every manifest, published, installed, re-locked by hunsu and loaded by a new session.
7. Codex limitations, each observed on this machine:
 a. A Claude Code session started from a Codex parent inherits CODEX_THREAD_ID; chongdae 1.24.0 then records that session as host codex with the parent thread's model (chongdae.py `performer`: AGENT_HOST decides, else codex whenever CODEX_THREAD_ID is set). Export AGENT_HOST=claude-code in such a session before calling the engines. Seen in run-20261030-065818-2049, task adopt-env (its record names `codex gpt-6-astra`; commit 4de6d33's message carries the correction).
 b. `AGENT_HOST=codex hunsu check` exits 1 with "content differs" for hunsu, mangsang and jokbo: Codex's installs of those three carry a root `.codex-marketplace-install.json` that hunsu 1.15.1 counts in its content fingerprint. Pending a hunsu repair; do not `--take-content` past it. The Claude-host `hunsu check` passes.
 c. Codex project hooks (`.codex/hooks.json`) are written only by `hunsu lock` run from a Codex session; this project has none. `{plugin:NAME}` resolves through Claude's install records; Codex-only installs need hunsu.local.json links (README#limits).
8. mangsang has no model here yet: no concepts, nothing registered, so `mangsang impact` reporting 0 unresolved means nothing is watched, not coverage.

The check additionally requires these literal strings somewhere in the file: >=3.11, N+1, AGENT_HOST=claude-code, CODEX_THREAD_ID, .codex-marketplace-install.json, init --session, dakdol, teujip, sibi, chojja, eyes_worker, dwitbuk review, mangsang impact; each locked plugin name followed closely by its version; links to AGENTS.md, README.md, hunsu.json, hunsu.lock.json, skills/run/SKILL.md; no trailing whitespace; a final newline.
